physical_skill: Close each doll by pressing its top square down a snug friction fit (about 10 N for the 150 mm doll, 5 N for the 103 mm doll) with its face turned to the apron (before or by twisting against the fit), with the inner doll closed and dropped inside first, carrying the closed doll by its head through the fit into the next bottom half with about 2 mm of play, then closing the outer doll over it and letting go.
valid_shortcuts: None that score: do nothing 0; set tops on without pressing (they rest 5-7 mm up) 0.25; press tops on without turning (faces 90 degrees off) 0.25; keep holding the last top 0.75; close doll 2 outside doll 1 and close doll 1 empty 0.5. One arm could in principle do every step (each press is against the table); the task does not claim two-handedness.
distinct_from_nearest: A friction-fit closure of hollow coaxial shells that must be pressed and turned to a face, repeated in nested order, carrying a closed doll by its fit; nearest board tasks are single lids or hubs without nesting or orientation. Residual risk: reviewers may view lid closing as covered (press/snap-fit family) or judge relatability afresh.
